newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates steady to firm for Far East.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates steady to firm for Far East.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were mostly steady on Thursday with tonnage to the Far East showing the only spark in an otherwise lacklustre market.
The Middle East Gulf/Far East route appeared to buck the market with rates holding up at higher levels after leaping earlier this week from W57.5 for tonnage to Japan to W67.

"There is no improvement apart from the AG. That seems to be the only real one. We had a jump a few days ago and it has remained around there. That's about the only decent things that has happened," a broker said.
Enquiries were thin across the board and a broker said he was surprised rates were holding up elsewhere.
"A lot of people fixed ahead this year so the usual players will be quiet for the rest of the month," a broker said.
The Med was particularly subdued with cross-Med Aframax rates holding at W105. Suezmax fetched W90-W95 for modern ships, which brokers said were not in short supply.
"There are no enquiries in the Med. It's very quiet and we do not expect things to change this side of the weekend," a broker said.
"You could probably get a discount for older ships if you can find cargoes. There seems to be good supply which makes a nice change for picky charterers," the broker added.
"Levels are staying up and with the amount of enquiry coming in, you would think they would drop," another broker said.
He said the market could ease if older ships were offered at lower numbers but there was no sign of that yet. One vessel said fixed in the Med at W110 was later heard to have failed.
North Sea, Inter-UKC trade for 80,000 tonne business saw rates coming off slightly after earlier fixings this week at $112.5. Thursday's fixtures saw rates between W95 and W105.
